parole.testo: From Proto-Slavic *bagrъ (“treated with heat, thermic”). Originally an adjective, which later has been substantivized. The particular hue degree crimson may have been influenced by Oghur *băɣŭr < Proto-Turkic *bakïr (“copper, dirt”) (cf. Chuvash пӑхӑр (păh̬ăr, “copper”)), possibly of Iranian origin.

Continues Proto-Slavic *bělěgъ, ultimately of Oghur origin, from Proto-Turkic *bel- (“to denote”). Apparently, the Bulgarian term was reanalyzed to fit the Slavic morphology as if from Proto-Slavic *bělъ (“white”) + -ег (-eg).
